A projective object P lifts maps through every epimorphism in the chosen category.

A Verma flag does not specify all extension maps or the Loewy structure. Those require further information.

Two meanings of “finite-dimensional weight modules”

Finite-dimensional modules that are weight modules: for semisimple , this is just the finite-dimensional representation category. Weyl's theorem applies.

Possibly infinite modules with finite-dimensional weight spaces: this is a much larger category. It may also contain non-highest-weight simples. Ordinary -projectivity does not automatically extend to it. One must specify support conditions, finite generation, and whether the central character is exact or generalized.

For reductive with a nonzero center, finite-dimensional modules need not be semisimple unless the center acts semisimply. For solvable Lie algebras, Weyl's theorem does not apply.

Exact central character versus generalized central character

  • Generalized: every vector is killed by a sufficiently high power of .

The usual block uses the generalized condition. Fixing the character exactly can exclude ordinary projective covers: in , the central character acts nonsemisimply on .

A quotient algebra has free projective modules, but that does not imply its simple modules have projective covers. Covers need minimality, not just enough free modules.
